transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-08
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 40 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Sullivan (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Rakesh Patel (AstraNova ML Eng), Tina Morales (Platform Lead), Evelyn Park (CTO), Jonas Berg (Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on model variant selection, explicit version pinning, and fallback/rollback playbook. Reviewed recent benchmark numbers, discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality), agreed on temporary pin to v1.2 for gen routes with a quantized v1.0 fallback, and defined canary/rollback tests. Action items and schedule captured.

Topics:
- Catalog comparison: v1.0, v1.1-small, v1.2 (new topology)
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and observed tail latency spikes
- Pinning strategy and automated fallback triggers
- Security/observability for fallbacks (audit logs, alerts)
- Canary plan and success criteria

Action items (also captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok, hey everyone, thanks for making time. I think we have 40 minutes — quick agenda, bench numbers, pinning proposal, canary, rollbacks. Sound good?
[00:14] Rakesh Patel: yeah that works. thanks Maya. we've been seeing some variance overnight on the long call paths.
[00:22] Liam O'Sullivan: quick note — today's numbers are from the 10k request run we did wednesday night, mixed prompts, 8k short prompts, 2k long. i pushed the CSV to the drive, link in chat.
[00:35] Tina Morales: i got it, opening now.
[00:39] Jonas Berg: small ask up front — make sure any fallback events are audited; we need an immutable log for compliance.
[00:45] Maya Chen: totally, we can include trace IDs in the fallback payload and log to the private audit bucket. that was part of the private deployment checklist.
[00:54] [00:54] Speaker 3: (murmur) 
[00:56] Liam O'Sullivan: ok, so top-line: v1.2 gives 12-15% better quality on the red-team set but average latency is ~18% higher at median and the 99th percentile shows a couple of spikes to 1.5x. v1.0-quantized is cheaper and lower latency but some hallucination edges on the prompt set.
[01:20] Rakesh Patel: can you remind us what changed in v1.2 again? i know the layernorm tweak and different attention kernel but cmiiw.
[01:30] Liam O'Sullivan: yep, correct — it has a revised causal attention mapping and a small architecture tweak that increases compute per token; also upstream tokenizer santization fixes. it's why quality improves but costs climb.
[01:46] Evelyn Park: what's the delta on cost per 1000 tokens for v1.2 vs v1.0-quant? ballpark.
[01:52] Maya Chen: ballpark, v1.2 is ~22% higher cost per token on hosted; on Dedicated we see slight compression to ~15% because of batching gains.
[02:05] Tina Morales: and latency numbers under dedicated? that's what we care about — production region is us-west-2.
[02:12] Liam O'Sullivan: in our dedicated sim at us-west-2, median latency for v1.2 generation route is 160ms vs 135ms for v1.0-quant. 99p is 420ms vs 280ms respectively; those spikes are the concern.
[02:28] Rakesh Patel: are those spikes correlated with KV cache misses?
[02:32] Liam O'Sullivan: partly — we saw a strong correlation with cold KV cache windows and also with long self-attention runs for 1% of the prompts.
[02:42] Maya Chen: so our recommended approach is: pin to v1.2 for primary generation to get quality, but configure automatic fallback to v1.0-quantized when response latency > 700ms or when error rate crosses 2% for route X. that way SLA holds and we keep quality most of the time.
[03:02] Rakesh Patel: sounds reasonable. what about metric drift — i.e., if v1.2 starts degrading on certain prompt families, how do we detect and roll back?
[03:12] Liam O'Sullivan: we recommend a small continuous eval — we can run 500 eval prompts hourly, compute BLEU/accuracy-like scores and alert if drop > 3% relative to baseline. rollback can be manual or automated depending on comfort level; we can do a canary first.
[03:29] Tina Morales: canary details? i assume you want a canary with maybe 1% of traffic or synthetic traffic?
[03:35] Maya Chen: both options are available. our suggestion: 5% real traffic for 2 hours in staging (mirror) then a 2-hour controlled ramp in production with synthetic load targeting failure modes. default traffic shift is 5 -> 20 -> 100 if metrics look good.
[03:52] Jonas Berg: on security, we need to ensure fallback events are visible in our SIEM and the user tokens are masked. also, who owns the alert?
[04:03] Priya Nair: Redwood can push alert hooks to your PagerDuty or Slack and include minimal context — trace id, route, reason (latency/error). we can separate alert severity.
[04:15] Evelyn Park: fine. can we also make sure the logs are searchable for audits.
[04:20] Maya Chen: yes — we'll add an audit log export to your S3 with lifecycle rules; retention per your policy.
[04:27] [05:00] Liam O'Sullivan: going back to model selection — given AstraNova's quality bar (low hallucination tolerance), our recommendation is pinning v1.2 for the core summarization route and using v1.0-quant for lower-risk retrieval-augmented routes.
[05:15] Rakesh Patel: retrieval routes are high-volume, so cost matters there. pinning v1.0-quant sounds fine.
[05:22] Tina Morales: question — if we pin v1.2, can we still get quantized kernels for that model to reduce cost?
[05:29] Liam O'Sullivan: short answer: not yet for v1.2; the quantized kernel path exists for v1.0. we're evaluating quantization for v1.2 but it's an extra QA step and we haven't validated quality yet.
[05:43] Maya Chen: so for now we recommend hybrid: v1.2 pinned for sensitive gen routes, v1.0-quant for high-throughput retrievals.
[05:52] Rakesh Patel: ok. any experiments we should run to validate the fallback thresholds?
[05:58] Liam O'Sullivan: yes: we propose two experiments — 1) synthetic latency injection to verify fallback triggers under tail load, 2) quality regression test on the red-team prompts to validate fallbacks don't mask quality regressions.
[06:13] Tina Morales: synthetic injection — can you outline how intrusive that is? we don't want to destabilize production.
[06:19] Liam O'Sullivan: we'll do it in staging first; injection simply adds artificial delay to the kernel path for a subset of requests; it simulates KV-miss heavy traffic. then we'll validate automated rollback works and alerts trigger.
[06:31] Maya Chen: timeline — we can run staging injection this week, then a 2-hour canary next Monday in production window.
[06:38] Evelyn Park: what about rollback automation — is it atomic at route level or more coarse?
[06:43] Liam O'Sullivan: route-level is supported. we can do route pin swaps and instant traffic reroutes. the playbook we'll share includes runbook commands for a quick revert.
[06:55] [07:00] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) 
[07:02] Rakesh Patel: one operational ask — can we get per-token cost broken down by route + quantization delta?
[07:09] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include per-route cost in the CSV and show cost delta by quantization state.
[07:17] Tina Morales: also need token accounting for the call context since some routes include long context windows.
[07:23] Liam O'Sullivan: noted; our token breakdown will include average context length and peak memory windows.
[07:30] Jonas Berg: security follow-up — can you confirm KMS key ownership model when Redwood is hosting vs Dedicated?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Quick summary: hosted -- Redwood-managed KMS by default with customer-managed KMS available on enterprise plans; Dedicated/Private supports customer KMS only and HSM options. we'll attach doc.
[07:50] Evelyn Park: we need the Hosted KMS parity doc; that's one of our procurement checks.
[07:55] Maya Chen: will share.
[08:00] Liam O'Sullivan: ok, moving to rollback thresholds — recommended defaults: latency>700ms sustained over 5 minutes OR error rate > 2% over 5 minutes triggers automated fallback to v1.0-quant for route X. manual rollback if quality alerts > 3% degradation.
[08:22] Rakesh Patel: can we tune those thresholds? some of our long-context calls sometimes hit 650ms and that's normal.
[08:29] Liam O'Sullivan: absolutely — thresholds are tunable per-route. for summarization route we might raise the threshold to 850ms to account for expected long-context latency.
[08:40] Maya Chen: we'll propose per-route thresholds in the spreadsheet — default and suggested tuned.
[08:48] [09:00] Tina Morales: do we have observability for per-request model variant? i.e., can we see which model served a particular user request?
[09:07] Priya Nair: yes, trace IDs include model id, variant tag, and kernel hash. search by trace id in the Console.
[09:15] Evelyn Park: great. also please include how model rollouts affect token billing.
[09:21] Maya Chen: we'll show billing delta in the report.
[09:24] [09:30] Speaker 3: (inaudible) 
[09:31] Liam O'Sullivan: small note on fallbacks — there's an option to degrade gracefully by sending partial output or shorter sequences; we don't recommend for AstraNova's use-case because it can affect downstream UI, but it's available.
[09:48] Rakesh Patel: downstream EHR ingestion expects full output — partials are a no-go.
[09:52] Maya Chen: understood. fallback will be full response from the fallback model, not partial.
[09:58] Tina Morales: ok next, can we review the experiment results quick?
[10:02] Liam O'Sullivan: sure — i'll call out three slices: short prompts (<64 tokens), medium (64-256), long (>256). short prompts had no 99p issues; medium had occasional 99p spikes for v1.2; long prompts produced the majority of the tail.
[10:19] Rakesh Patel: what's the failure mode for long prompts — OOMs or slow self-attention?
[10:24] Liam O'Sullivan: mostly self-attention compute and some KV cache coldness — KV cache helps when you have repeated prefixes but we saw many unique long prompts.
[10:35] Maya Chen: recommended mitigation: restrict long-prompt routes to Dedicated pools with higher memory, and enable stronger prefix caching for repeated session flows.
[10:45] Tina Morales: Dedicated pricing — is there a minimum commitment? we need to see if it makes sense for our expected throughput.
[10:51] Maya Chen: there's a dedicated baseline; i'll include cost comparisons for committed vs burst.
[10:56] Evelyn Park: procurement will want an estimated burn rate.
[11:00] Maya Chen: we'll provide a 90-day projection based on your traffic profile.
[11:05] [11:15] Jonas Berg: on compliance — can the fallback flag be redacted from user logs to avoid leaking model internals to downstream BI?
[11:20] Priya Nair: yes, fields can be redacted. we'll share the schema of the logs.
[11:26] Rakesh Patel: any plan for automated regression tests pre-rollout?
[11:30] Liam O'Sullivan: yes — the continuous eval suite runs nightly and we can gate rollouts behind passing the suite for key metrics.
[11:38] Tina Morales: how do we measure hallucination for our tasks? do you support custom metrics?
[11:43] Liam O'Sullivan: you can plug in custom metrics — e.g., entity-fidelity score; we can accept your script or run our built-in metrics.
[11:50] Mayer Chen: (laughs) maya typo —
[11:52] Maya Chen: haha, all good.
[11:54] [12:00] Liam O'Sullivan: final operational piece: auto-fallback telemetry will emit a normal event and an alert event when threshold is hit. we recommend a two-tier alerting model: warn (metric drift) and critical (auto-fallback executed).
[12:16] Tina Morales: ok, i think we're aligned. can we capture a short runbook for manual rollback?
[12:22] Maya Chen: absolutely — in the playbook we'll include one-click rollback steps and CLI commands with safety checks.
[12:30] Rakesh Patel: timeline recap?
[12:33] Maya Chen: share spreadsheet by 7/9, staging injection 7/10, customer prompt set by 7/11, canary 7/14, rollback doc by 7/13.
[12:44] Evelyn Park: agreed.
[12:46] [13:00] Speaker 3: 
[13:04] Liam O'Sullivan: any other risks we haven't covered?
[13:08] Jonas Berg: risk of model drift after upstream tokenizer patch — need to monitor tokenization diffs.
[13:14] Maya Chen: will add tokenization diff checks into the eval.
[13:19] Rakesh Patel: small UX ask — can the Console mark requests that hit fallback so Product can show a subtle indicator?
[13:26] Priya Nair: yes, that's on the roadmap; we can flag fallback hits and export CSV for product.
[13:33] Tina Morales: perfect.
[13:35] Maya Chen: okay last thing — who owns the canary run on 7/14 from AstraNova side?
[13:41] Rakesh Patel: i'll coordinate infra, Tina will own product-level success criteria, Evelyn will sign off on go/no-go.
[13:49] Maya Chen: great. we'll send calendar invite for the canary window.
[13:55] [14:00] Liam O'Sullivan: i'll follow up with the rollback playbook and the fallback test script.
[14:04] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. quick recap: pin v1.2 for sensitive gen, v1.0-quant for retrieval, run staging injection, gather red-team prompts, schedule canary 7/14. action items in the shared doc.
[14:18] Evelyn Park: thanks. bye.
[14:20] Meeting end.
